messages.subject: blavaan - latent change score models
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,
thank you for a great package and great ressources!
I wondered whether it is already possible to apply bivariate latent change score models in blavaan?
Thanks!

efficiency. A good resource for code is the osf page below... they

Ed

messages.subject: Approximate MI using Rstan
messages.body_plain:
Hello:
I am trying to test approximate MI using blavaan by following your previous post:
https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/blavaan/9hRwHucBFJs/discussion
 I am using stan instead of jags.
However, it seems that the argument:  mcmcextra=list() is not available for stan...I got an error message:

Error in blavaan(MG.M, data = sam2, group = "MALE", std.lv <http://std.lv> = TRUE, do.fit = FALSE,  :
  blavaan ERROR: mcmcextra is not available for target='stan'

Is it possible to do Approximate MI using stan ?
Thanks!
Best
Rui

messages.subject: Re: Approximate MI using Rstan
messages.body_plain:
Rui,

It is on the list of things to implement in Stan, but it is not
currently available. For now, one option would be to set
mcmcfile=TRUE, then edit the resulting Stan file to build it yourself.
The procedure described in the blog post below seems relevant:

https://statmodeling.stat.columbia.edu/2019/08/23/yes-you-can-include-prior-information-on-quantities-of-interest-not-just-on-parameters-in-your-model/

Ed

messages.subject: Re: Approximate MI using Rstan
messages.body_plain:
Rui

You can do approximate MI with Stan, but with the stanclassic model, instead of the current default stan model. This means that will be slower.
You can use the trick of using the name of the parameter for group 1 as the mean of the prior for group 2, here is an example

library(blavaan)
library(rstan)
rstan_options(auto_write = TRUE)
options(mc.cores = parallel::detectCores())

################################################################################
## data import

dat <- read.csv("Grade7.csv")
head(dat)

#########################
### configural invariance
mod1 <- '
Positive =~ PosAFF1 + PosAFF2 + PosAFF3
Agency =~ Agency1 + Agency2 + Agency3
            '

## Stan
fit1_stan <-  bcfa(mod1, data=dat, std.lv <http://std.lv>=T, group="Gender",
                   n.chains = 3, burnin=5000,
                   sample=5000, target="stanclassic")
summary(fit1_stan, standardized=T,rsquare=T,postmedian=TRUE)

#######################
#### Approximate weak invariance

#### check Stan syntax parameter names
with(parTable(fit1_stan), cbind(lhs,op,rhs,pxnames))

#### when std.lv <http://std.lv>=T, need to use lambdaUNC instead of lambda
## Stan
mod2_ap_stan <- '
Positive =~ prior(c("","normal(lambdaUNC[1,1,1],.1)"))*PosAFF1 +
            prior(c("","normal(lambdaUNC[2,1,1],.1)"))*PosAFF2 +
            prior(c("","normal(lambdaUNC[3,1,1],.1)"))*PosAFF3
Agency =~ prior(c("","normal(lambdaUNC[4,2,1],.1)"))*Agency1 +
            prior(c("","normal(lambdaUNC[5,2,1],.1)"))*Agency2 +
            prior(c("","normal(lambdaUNC[6,2,1],.1)"))*Agency3

Positive ~~ c(1, NA)*Positive
Agency ~~ c(1, NA)*Agency
            '

fit2_ap_stan <-  bcfa(mod2_ap_stan, data=dat, std.lv <http://std.lv>=T,
                      group="Gender",
                      n.chains = 3, burnin=5000,
                      sample=5000, target="stanclassic" )
summary(fit2_ap_stan, standardized=T,rsquare=T,postmedian=TRUE)

#########################
###### Approximate Strong Invariance

#### check Stan syntax parameter names
with(parTable(fit1_stan), cbind(lhs,op,rhs,pxnames))

## Stan
mod3_ap_stan <- '
Positive =~ prior(c("","normal(lambdaUNC[1,1,1],.1)"))*PosAFF1 +
            prior(c("","normal(lambdaUNC[2,1,1],.1)"))*PosAFF2 +
            prior(c("","normal(lambdaUNC[3,1,1],.1)"))*PosAFF3
Agency =~ prior(c("","normal(lambdaUNC[4,2,1],.1)"))*Agency1 +
            prior(c("","normal(lambdaUNC[5,2,1],.1)"))*Agency2 +
            prior(c("","normal(lambdaUNC[6,2,1],.1)"))*Agency3

Positive ~~ c(1, NA)*Positive
Agency ~~ c(1, NA)*Agency

Positive ~c(0,NA)*1
Agency ~c(0,NA)*1

PosAFF1 ~prior(c("","normal(nu[1,1,1],.1)"))*1
PosAFF2 ~prior(c("","normal(nu[2,1,1],.1)"))*1
PosAFF3 ~prior(c("","normal(nu[3,1,1],.1)"))*1
Agency1 ~prior(c("","normal(nu[4,1,1],.1)"))*1
Agency2 ~prior(c("","normal(nu[5,1,1],.1)"))*1
Agency3 ~prior(c("","normal(nu[6,1,1],.1)"))*1
            '

fit3_ap_stan <-  bcfa(mod3_ap_stan, data=dat, std.lv <http://std.lv>=T,
                      group="Gender",
                      n.chains = 3, burnin=5000,
                      sample=5000, target="stanclassic" )
summary(fit3_ap_stan, standardized=T,rsquare=T,postmedian=TRUE)
